sections.h2: Who bills, values and sets the rate in Long County?
sections.html:
Three offices share the job in Ludowici, and all three sit on McDonald Street. One sets values, one sends and collects bills, and one votes the county rate.

  • Long County Tax Assessor's Office: 285 S McDonald St, Ludowici, GA 31316. Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm. Phone (912) 545-9111. Its page links to the qPublic parcel search and a digest archive that goes back to 2016.
  • Long County Tax Commissioner: P.O. Box 628, 285 South McDonald Street, Ludowici, GA 31316. Phone 912-545-2127. Payments now run through a newer site, and the older taxpayer search tab no longer takes them.
  • Long County Board of Commissioners: 468 S. McDonald Street, Ludowici. It adopts the county millage rate at a called meeting, and the office works Monday through Thursday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, closed on Fridays since January 26, 2026.

State guidance from the Department of Revenue sorts the questions this way: bills and payments go to the commissioner, while value, exemption and appeal questions go to the assessors. If you call the wrong desk, expect a quick referral.

sections.h2: Why does growth matter to a Long County seller?
sections.html:
Long County is rural and mostly farm and forest, roughly 400 square miles with Ludowici as its single city and county seat. The county's history page traces the farm economy from cotton to tobacco, corn, soybeans and cattle, with pine timber and nearby paper mills supplying steady work.

Fort Stewart, the largest military installation east of the Mississippi River, occupies the northern tip and provides civil service jobs for residents. Altamaha Technical College keeps a satellite campus in Ludowici. Long County School System covers the public schools, apart from the base, where the Department of Defense Education Activity runs the elementary level.

The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 21,557 residents, against 16,168 in the 2020 count. QuickFacts lists 7,798 housing units, and about two of every three homes are lived in by their owners (65.2%). Homes that owners occupy have a middle value of $218,300, and the average commute takes 29.8 minutes.

Aimar, Beards Creek, Donald and Tibet are unincorporated, so owners there go to the county rather than a city hall for permits and tax questions. Liberty, McIntosh, Wayne and Tattnall counties border Long County.

sections.h2: How has the Long County tax digest changed since 2021?
sections.html:
The county's published five-year history shows a taxable base that keeps growing and a county rate that moves in steps. The net digest rose from about $328.8 million in 2021 to about $546.0 million in the 2026 figures, with a net maintenance and operation millage of 17.802 mills in the 2026 presentation.

2021$328,796,57315.597

2023$391,934,56514.738
2024$402,074,61318.707

2026$546,043,75317.802

Source: the 2026 Tax Digest and 5 Year History published by the Long County Board of Commissioners. The notice says the levy reflects reductions from Property Tax Relief Local Option Sales Tax proceeds, also called FLOST, applied against property tax. County voters authorized FLOST in 2025, and the combined sales tax rate in Long County became 9% on January 1, 2026.

For the 2025 rate, the assessors' page carried a notice of a tentative increase of 20.72 percent: 18.707 mills against 15.496 mills without the increase, with hearings on February 12 and February 19, 2026. A called meeting on September 24, 2026 was scheduled to adopt the 2026 millage. School and state levies sit on top of the county figure, so use the rate shown on your own bill.

The same publication splits the 2026 digest into a gross figure of $791,914,814 and exemptions of $245,871,061, which leaves the net value in the table. Exemptions stood at $104,458,820 in 2024 and $234,837,877 in 2025, so the jump in the net base in 2025 came with a much larger exempt share. Real and personal property made up $774,693,757 of the 2026 gross, while motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber were small slices.

sections.h2: When are Long County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Recent Long County due dates have followed the digest rather than a fixed calendar date. For the 2025 bills, the tax commissioner's page listed real estate taxes due May 12, 2026, and mobile home taxes due June 1, 2026 in place of the usual April 1, because the digest came out late.

The state default is December 20 with 60 days from billing, and a county may choose another date. Check the due date shown on each bill, and ask the commissioner's office when the next mailing goes out.

  • Property returns are due in the window that opens January 1 and closes April 1.
  • Mobile home tax is normally due April 1.
  • Payment runs through the newer payment site linked from the commissioner's page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Long County assessment?
sections.html:
You get 45 days after the notice goes out in the mail. Put the appeal on paper for the Long County assessors, using the uniform form the state provides.

That first filing is where you pick a route: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue officials have no power to overrule any of those bodies, or Superior Court, on one property's appraisal. Where a county has adopted a written policy accepting electronic service, the appeal may be emailed, and the assessors can say if Long County has done so. Their page lists longcoappr@longcountyga.gov.

Valid grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, equal treatment with similar parcels, or a turned-down exemption. Before filing, pull your parcel on qPublic and compare it with recent sales nearby.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Long County?
sections.html:
The standard state homestead exemption knocks $2,000 off the assessed value, which Georgia sets at 40% of market value. The home must be your main residence.

  • Some counties take homestead filings at the commissioner's desk and others at the assessors. Ask Long County which one applies.
  • Local exemptions can exceed the state one. The assessors can list them with their age and income limits.
  • Farm, timber and conservation assessments rest on a covenant signed with the assessors, so confirm eligibility before assuming acreage qualifies.

Census data show 275 building permits in Long County for 2025. New construction and added improvements feed the digest, so compare your January 1 value with the parcel record.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Long County tax when you sell?
sections.html:
The January 1 title holder owes the full year, and a sale on January 2 changes nothing with the state. No refund goes to partial-year owners, so buyer and seller divide the bill in the contract.

Ask the commissioner for a payoff amount that includes interest or penalty, and hand the closing attorney the current bill. If the county has recorded a tax lien (a fi fa) against the parcel, payoff or release is needed before a buyer can take clean title.

An inherited, behind-on-tax or tenant-occupied house in Long County follows the same steps. Call early, since a figure quoted weeks ahead can grow as interest adds up.

faqs.q: Which Long County office answers questions about my bill?
faqs.a: Billing and payment questions go to the Tax Commissioner at 912-545-2127, or by mail to P.O. Box 628 in Ludowici. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office at (912) 545-9111.

faqs.q: How long is the Long County assessment appeal window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. File on paper with the county assessors and name your chosen route in that first filing.

faqs.q: Has the Long County millage rate gone up?
faqs.a: The published history shows net M&O millage of 14.738 in 2023, 18.707 in 2024 and 2025, and 17.802 in the 2026 presentation. Sales tax relief proceeds were applied against the levy, so use the rate on your bill.

faqs.q: Is any tax refunded when a Long County home sells mid-year?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 owner owes the whole year, so the buyer and seller settle the split in the sales contract.

faqs.q: Where can I search a Long County parcel online?
faqs.a: Use the qPublic property search linked from the Tax Assessor's page. It shows parcel records, and the assessors' office can explain any value you find.
